::: {#def-gan}

#### Generative adversarial network (GAN)

A **generative adversarial network**,
or **GAN**,
has a generator $G$,
which maps a draw $\vz$ of noise to a data point $G(\vz)$,
and a discriminator $D$,
which gives the probability $D(\vx)$ that a data point $\vx$ is real.
They are trained in turn,
$D$ to maximize and $G$ to minimize

$$
V(D, G) = \E{\logf{D(X)}} + \E{\logf{1 - D(G(\vecf{Z}))}},
$$

where $X$ is a real data point and $\vecf{Z}$ is the noise
[@goodfellow2014generative, section 3].
@goodfellow2014generative [section 3] train $G$ to maximize $\logf{D(G(\vecf{Z}))}$ instead,
which gives larger [gradients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) early in training,
when $D$ rejects the made-up points easily.

:::
